solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Long-distance traveller may get this nice hire-car from Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase trades its initial consonants

blocks.note: to hire is to let; it takes the opening sound of the other word
a Jag (Jaguar) is a smart British car; it takes the opening sound of the other word
padding that marks the car as a posh make

explanation.surface: A long-haul traveller is offered a smart rental car on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: LET JAG with its first sounds exchanged becomes JET LAG. Jag is the British nickname for a Jaguar, a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing many time zones by plane leaves the body clock out of step, the tiredness flyers suffer after arrival.

clue.text: Online fraud taking half of the writer’s finances, etc

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, so only its front letter is kept

blocks.note: E- is the prefix for online, as in email
a con is a swindle
the first half of the little word
the writer speaking of himself says my

explanation.surface: An internet scam grabs a share of the author's money and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' looks like it applies to 'the writer's', but it halves only the word 'of'. E-CON is an online fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's or household's economy is its management of money, resources, budgets and spending.

clue.text: Ample bill of fare: ordered off this

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are put into a new sequence
the word printed just before is taken off the phrase, so its letters come out

blocks.note: taken as written, the menu phrase

explanation.surface: A generous menu: you choose and order from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O, F, F (the word 'off') from BILL OF FARE, then rearrange BILLARE. A bill of fare is a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal helpings are generous or plentiful ones, so the adjective is a synonym for abundant.

clue.text: Mercury rising essentially spoiled butter

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading from bottom to top
the essence of a word is its core, so its central letter is kept

blocks.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: As the thermometer climbs, the butter goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercury rising' reads like a heatwave, which would spoil butter; here it is a chemical symbol written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghi, also spelt ghee, is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Marks what winning run will do in series down under?

blocks.note: the winning run finishes the match
the Ashes is the England v Australia Test cricket series, here played in Australia

explanation.surface: Scores what a decisive run achieves in a cricket series in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like a verb about scoring; it is a noun. END ASHES is then respaced as EN DASHES.
explanation.definitionFit: En dashes are punctuation marks, the short dash used for ranges like 1990–95.

clue.text: Oddly make Mensa gift out of FT puzzles

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters fall in an unusual order
out of here means taken away from, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A strange way for Mensa to present a gift, using the FT's crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters; it is the anagram signal. Remove F and T from MENSA GIFT and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are riddles or mysteries, things that baffle and need solving.

clue.text: Two Germans find 22’s clue complicated aerial combat

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so its letters are mixed up

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German, taken twice
taken as written
the clue to 22-across reads Hit Go

explanation.surface: Two German visitors find another clue in this puzzle hard to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies letters: the words of the 22-across clue join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogfighting is close-range combat between fighter aircraft, twisting and turning in the sky.

clue.text: Censure disc and album covers

indicators.note: what covers something has it inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of disc, all of and, and the start of album

explanation.surface: Criticism of a record and the artwork on its sleeves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' suggests album sleeves, but it is the signal that the answer is inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage scandal means defamatory talk or public reproach, so it overlaps with criticism.

clue.text: Back the last ’ack in the race

indicators.note: the apostrophe marks a dropped aitch in Cockney speech, so the H sound goes

blocks.note: the last part is the end
a runner in the race is a horse, said Cockney-fashion

explanation.surface: A punter backs the final nag in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ack is hack with its H dropped, telling you to say the runner the same way: 'orse.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support it publicly, which is to back it.

clue.text: Dull exertion that keeps books to the fore?

definitions.text: Dull exertion that keeps books to the fore?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, and 'to the fore' places it near the front

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical mark for soft or muted
oiling the works, the effort of keeping something running
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books, and B is book

explanation.surface: Tedious labour that keeps a writer's titles in the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a potboiler is a book written fast for money, to keep the pot boiling. The wordplay is loose, and some solvers read PO TOILING around B instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing potboilers is uninspired commercial work done to pay the bills, which keeps new titles coming.

clue.text: Puts in PS something cutting from Mike?

indicators.note: a mike is a microphone, so what comes from it is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: an adze is a cutting tool like an axe

explanation.surface: Someone tacks a postscript onto a letter with something cutting from Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a man's name; it is a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a postscript is putting extra remarks at the end of a letter, which is what one adds.

clue.text: Nothing in apart from pork

definitions.note: pork is the meat; the answer is the animal it may come from

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it

blocks.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: There is nothing on the menu except pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from' looks like part of the surface phrase; it is the word BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig, the animal whose flesh supplies meat of that kind.

clue.text: They’re left memoranda, the last of which is penetrating

indicators.note: what penetrates goes into something, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: memos are notes to jog the memory
'which' points back to the memoranda, whose final letter is A

explanation.surface: Notes left behind for someone, the last one being incisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' refers back to the previous word, so its last letter is taken from that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Remainders are what is left over, including unsold books sold off cheaply by publishers.

clue.text: Somehow managed Duke’s Head lounge bar, moving round barrels

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so its opening letter is kept
letters that are moving shift out of their places
to go round something is to surround it

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written
b is an abbreviation for barrel in the drinks trade

explanation.surface: Somehow the landlord ran the lounge bar of the Duke's Head pub, rolling the barrels about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke's Head' reads as a pub name; it gives one letter. The rearranged letters go round B.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub along is a British idiom for coping or getting by without great success.

clue.text: Membership accepting associate reviewed course outline

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in
re-viewed suggests viewed again from the other end

blocks.note: subs are the subscriptions paid for membership
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A club admits a colleague after reviewing the course plan.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBS holds ALLY, and the whole is written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus lists the topics a programme of study will cover, its summary plan.

clue.text: Principal leaves the lecturer with an assistant

indicators.note: the principal letter is the first, and it leaves, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: the word loses its front letter
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer
as in ten pounds an hour, meaning per hour

explanation.surface: The head teacher departs, leaving the lecturer with a teaching assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like a head teacher; here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who aids another, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In correspondence about the last of the repeats

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: on means concerning, as in a talk on art
its final letter
the chunk built so far, written out a second time

explanation.surface: A letter mentions something about the end of the reruns.
explanation.walkthrough: ON plus E makes ONE, and 'repeats' says write it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-one correspondence in mathematics pairs each member of one set with exactly one member of another.

clue.text: Commander Castro perhaps upset king on stage

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down answer that reads upwards

blocks.note: Fidel Castro was from Cuba; 'perhaps' marks him as an example
CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: A military leader, perhaps Castro, overthrows a monarch in a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed nationality comes first even though the commander is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabucco is Verdi's opera about Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian ruler, a monarch seen in theatres.

clue.text: Discover allusions hiding throughout

indicators.note: what is hiding something conceals it within

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Find references concealed all through a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throughout' looks like it belongs to 'hiding'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall can mean everywhere or in every part, as in covered overall, matching all through.

clue.text: A bit surreptitious, stealing land

indicators.note: a thief stealing something takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: sly means secretive
to light on is to land on, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: Someone a little furtive is grabbing territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun for territory; it is a verb, to light upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly is an adverb meaning to a small degree, the same as a little.

clue.text: Cheese list extends considerably, Palin’s close

indicators.note: to extend something is to stretch it apart, so another piece fills its middle
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is kept

blocks.note: so means very much, as in so tired
a ship that lists leans or tilts
its final letter

explanation.surface: A cheese menu grows a lot longer by the end of Palin's show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a noun; it is a verb, as a ship lists. 'extends' means stretched apart so another piece fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a classic English blue cheese named after a village in Cambridgeshire.

clue.text: This chap’s wrong about a cloth

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: this chap is he, so he's
a wrong is a sin
taken as written

explanation.surface: This fellow has misjudged a piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like an adjective; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse woven fabric of jute, used for sacks; Americans call it burlap.

clue.text: Hampton? What she wears from ground without trousers

indicators.note: starting from the ground in a down answer means reading upwards
to trouser something is to pocket it, so one piece takes in another

blocks.note: a goalkeeper wears shirt No 1
less means without, as in meat-less

explanation.surface: A woman playing football out on the pitch with no trousers on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a garment; it is a verb, to pocket. Hannah Hampton keeps goal for England's women's football team, who wear No 1 shirts in goal.
explanation.definitionFit: England's women's football team are nicknamed the Lionesses, so Hampton is one of them; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Holding information back, decrease in denial?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state, standing for a participle

indicators.note: going back means reading from the other end
to hold something is to keep it inside

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
abating means lessening

explanation.surface: Someone withholding facts, perhaps shrinking into denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding information back' reads as secrecy, but it is the wordplay frame; GEN is British slang for facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnegating means renouncing or rejecting, practising self-denial.

clue.text: Hit “Go”

blocks.note: first meaning: a strike
second meaning: a turn or attempt

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like an instruction to press a button; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a strike at a target and an attempt or turn at something.

clue.text: Proceedings logged on and off in Alcatraz?

indicators.note: something on and off works intermittently, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Records kept intermittently in the famous island prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'logged on' looks like computer jargon; 'on and off' is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is a Latin word for official records of the business of a body, minutes.

clue.text: Sent to Coventry: leaving by taxi, crossed Barking

indicators.note: what is leaving goes away, so those letters are removed
barking means mad, and mad letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
x means by, as in two by four
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shunned, someone takes a cab across Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like the London place name; it is British slang for mad. 'Sent to Coventry' is a British idiom for being deliberately ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ostracised is to be excluded and cold-shouldered by a group, as the idiom describes.

clue.text: Writer uses it to join double helix up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: DNA has a double-helix structure

explanation.surface: An author connects the two strands of a DNA molecule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join' sounds like biology linking strands; here it is grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction links words and clauses, the commonest connective in writing.

clue.text: Basis for cosmetic treatments filmmaker has cheek to inject on counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite, so it runs the other way
to inject is to put inside

blocks.note: the Coen brothers are American filmmakers
gall means impudence

explanation.surface: A film director has the nerve to give injections over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inject' fits the cosmetic surface; it signals one piece inside another. 'cheek' suggests a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Collagen is a structural protein injected into skin and lips as a filler in beauty treatments.

clue.text: Ultimately Trawlerman is had, taking a beating from Scandinavia

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is kept
something beaten is knocked out of shape

blocks.note: its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the end a fisherman is fooled and thrashed by Nordic rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' looks like being cheated; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian country, so its people and products are Nordic.
